purpose: Before/after performance for percentage letter/word spacing native-parser integration, relative to the selector-cache stage.

method.frequency_control: Uncontrolled boost/governor; shared machine. Paired sampling reduces drift, but intervals do not model systematic host interference.
method.compiler: rustc opt-level=2 debuginfo=0, identical frozen native dependencies and support crates on both sides
method.ci_method: 5000 bootstrap resamples of paired percentage changes; deterministic seed 173, median, 2.5/97.5 percentiles; no multiple-comparison adjustment. Diagnostic evidence, not a universal performance claim.
method.combined_metric: all_samples sums the five sample medians per invocation; it is cumulative sample time, not a simultaneous page or peak.
method.spacing_workloads: Existing EPUB benchmark source unchanged. Both use 64 classes at font-size:16px with prior length fallbacks. The output-equivalent workload uses letter-spacing:0% and word-spacing:calc(2px - 6.25%); the added-feature workload uses 2% and calc(2px + 5%). Baseline ignores new percentage declarations; changed build applies them. Both measure added feature work, not equivalent parsing behavior.

method.frequency_control: Uncontrolled boost/governor; shared machine. Paired sampling reduces drift, but intervals do not model systematic host interference.
method.compiler: rustc opt-level=2 debuginfo=0, identical frozen native dependencies and support crates on both sides
method.previous_stage_candidate_workload_not_us: Existing EPUB benchmark source unchanged; CSS fixtures replaced with 64 classes using counter-reset, counter-increment, content:counter(), and :has(p). Forms valid and rendered equivalently in both builds.
method.ci_method: 5000 bootstrap resamples of paired percentage changes; deterministic seed 173, median, 2.5/97.5 percentiles; no multiple-comparison adjustment. Diagnostic evidence, not a universal performance claim.
method.previous_stage_fallback_workload_not_use: Same candidate CSS plus flex-basis:min-content and z-index:calc(3 - 2). Baseline ignores these declarations; the changed build applies them. This measures added feature cost, not equivalent-output regression.
method.combined_metric: all_samples sums the five sample medians per invocation; it is cumulative sample time, not a simultaneous page or peak.
method.spacing_workloads: Existing EPUB benchmark source unchanged. Both use 64 classes at font-size:16px with prior length fallbacks. The output-equivalent workload uses letter-spacing:0% and word-spacing:calc(2px - 6.25%); the added-feature workload uses 2% and calc(2px + 5%). Baseline ignores new percentage declarations; changed build applies them. Both measure added feature work, not equivalent parsing behavior.

interpretation: Positive percentages mean slower. Intervals containing zero are inconclusive, not evidence of equivalence.

Both spacing workloads measure added feature work: the baseline ignores the new declarations, while the changed build parses and applies them. The first is designed to retain the same used spacings via explicit prior fallbacks; this does not establish equivalent parser work or pixel equality.
The changed-output workload uses nonzero percentages and mixed calculations. No renderer image suite was run.
Standalone percentages reuse the native percentage token directly. Mixed expressions still serialize/reparse during eligibility preparation and declaration application; all costs are retained.
Shared-host load/frequency and code layout affect timings. Intervals are diagnostic and have no multiple-comparison adjustment.
